sources.entry: Takeline - Fork of Textream that follows your voice in French and English entirely on the Mac, with retake detection and voice commands. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Bouliw/takeline) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Takeline is a macOS teleprompter that shows your script under the notch and highlights each word as you speak, in French and English, with on-device speech recognition.
summary.what_it_does: Takeline displays a script in a window pinned below the MacBook notch, as a floating window, fullscreen, or on an external display or Sidecar iPad, and highlights each word as it is spoken. It offers three guidance modes: word tracking using the microphone, classic constant-speed scrolling, and voice-activated scrolling. Speech recognition runs on the Mac through Apple's SpeechAnalyzer, and the README states that audio is not sent to a server. Retake phrases such as "take two" or re-reading a sentence send the text back to the start of that sentence and log the time. Voice commands cover previous paragraph, from the top, pause, resume, and text size. A remote view in a browser (access code in a QR code) and a Director mode for a script written from another browser are included. Scripts can be imported from PowerPoint notes, Word, Markdown, text, and .textream files.
use_cases: Reading a script on camera while recording a video
Teleprompting a presentation from the MacBook notch
Reading scripts on a phone or tablet over the local network
Keeping the good takes from a recording session using session files
Practicing a French or English speech with live word tracking
Estimating video length from a script
how_to_run: Download Takeline.dmg from the latest release, open it and drag Takeline into Applications.
Open Takeline; on first launch, approve it in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Open Anyway.
In Settings › Voice, click Install next to each language you speak.
Build from source: open Textream/Textream.xcodeproj in Xcode 26 or later, choose the Textream scheme and My Mac, then Product → Run.
notable: Fork of Textream that adds French and English word tracking with retake detection and voice commands
Speech recognition runs on the Mac; when a language is missing, it reports that rather than using a server
Session files (.takeline.json) save the script and every take for editing
Remote view and Director mode are protected by an access code and refuse devices outside the local network by default
Tracking, retake and import logic lives in a separate TakelineCore Swift package with tests
caveats: The app is not signed by an identified developer, so macOS requires a manual approval on first launch
Apple Intelligence is optional; without it, retake phrases are handled by simple rules
On iPhone or iPad with a free Apple account, an app installed from Xcode stops opening after 7 days
